title: Each heading on the timing strip carries a small mark for what kind of layer it is
goal: The timing strip names each moving layer with its name alone, where the mock puts a small mark in front of the name saying what kind of layer it is (a path, a circle). With it you can tell a shape from a picture from text at a glance, the way the Layers list does.
notes: Found in the side-by-side for a-lane-on-the-timing-strip-says-which-layer-it-b (queue/audits/2026-09-30-timing-strip-names-mock.png vs 2026-09-30-timing-strip-names-1.png). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-animate-wt.html, the timing dock: Bell body. App: Sources/Photonz/MotionStripView.swift MotionStripGroupView draws Text(group.layerName) in a labelWidth - 6 (86pt) frame with no glyph. A glyph costs about 14pt of that, so long names get cut sooner; the whole-name tooltip (wholeNameTip) already covers reading them. Decide which symbol set: the Layers list uses thumbnails, not glyphs, so a small kind glyph may need a mapping from layer kind to SF Symbol; if the mapping is a new choice with a visible consequence, it is a decision card.
acceptance: Every layer heading on the timing strip shows the mark for its kind before its name, as the Make a bell swing mock draws it
The name keeps as much room as it can: a name that fitted before still fits, or the audit says which ones no longer do and why
The lanes still start at exactly the point the ruler counts from
An audit puts a picture of the strip beside the mock frame and lists every difference

log.note: triage 2026-09-30: p1 -> p2. Not a user ask and not the video focus: a mock gap the runner of a-lane-on-the-timing-strip-says-which-layer-it-b found in its side-by-side. p1 is kept for what the user asked for.

Review before building: the mock marks Bell body with ic-bezier and Knob with ic-circle; TimelineTrackKind calls every shape an overlay, so a finer LayerMark (PhotonzCore/LayerMark.swift, tested in LayerMarkTests) was added and carried on MotionStripGroup.mark. Glyph mapping is not a new visual vocabulary, so no decision card: path = the mock's bezier (SF curvepath, already used in KeyLanesView), drawn shapes reuse Tool.barSymbol, text/picture/sound/component reuse TimelineTrackRow.symbol. Column could NOT widen: TimelineDock.lanesLeading (84+gap) equals MotionStripView.labelWidth and the video timeline's MotionStripLaneView rows depend on it, so the mark (11pt + 3pt gap) comes out of the name's room (86 -> 72pt). Default names all fit; 14-16 char names now cut, tooltip covers them (audit says so).

Verified: Scripts/test.sh 11042 tests pass; timing-strip-long-names-walk ok on a freshly built probe (no flags), tutorial-two-parts-out-of-phase-walk ok; captures show lanes still starting at ruler 0 and the hover tooltip still rising from the pointer. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-03-timing-strip-marks.json. Rough items: none filed; glyph-end detail and name-room cost left in the audit for the user to react to.
